message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS000753 is best supported by PRS-comparable evidence: it reports an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), and comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program). Competing models mostly report only full-model discrimination (e.g., AUROC/C-index) without PGS-only AUROC, which domain guidance cautions is not comparable for ranking; PGS001784 reports a covariates-regressed-out R2=0.014661 but is from a broad global biobank framework paper and its very high full-model AUROC (0.868) is likely covariate-driven given the heavy covariate set. PGS002054 is a portability-framework score with only partial-r=0.0144. PGS003972/PGS003973 are disease-focused but provide only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown/basic covariates and small validation sizes, leaving PRS-only contribution unclear. Overall, a direct-match exists, but lack of consistent PRS-only metrics across candidates and reliance on non-comparable full-model metrics keeps the recommendation sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength/clarity of reported PRS-relevant performance. PGS002738 is the best-supported direct-match because its trait_efo is exactly \"alcohol dependence\" and phenotyping_reported is \"Alcohol use disorder\" (a close clinical synonym for alcohol dependence), and it reports a reasonably strong discrimination-style effect metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900) with PRS-CS and multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB). The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC or PRS-only R2; PGS002738 also has unknown covariates and its effect-size reporting is not directly comparable to the ΔR² metrics reported for PGS000201/PGS000202. This leaves residual uncertainty in cross-model comparability, so the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001777","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis). PGS001777 is best supported because it is disease-focused (alcohol-related cirrhosis in drinkers) and provides the most PRS-informative discrimination evidence among the set via a large risk gradient (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, 95% CI 4.05–9.41) alongside an AUROC=0.671 in European evaluation. PGS000704 reports only a full-model C-index=0.711 with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), but lacks PRS-only metrics and shows only modest per-SD HR=1.18, making it unclear how much signal is attributable to the PRS versus covariates. PGS004913 reports a small R²=0.029 and OR top vs bottom deciles=4.4 but also lacks clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics and has smaller-scale evidence. Overall confidence is limited because none of the candidates reports explicit PRS-only AUROC, covariates are unknown for PGS001777, and the reported metrics are not directly comparable across differing study designs/endpoints."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported variants include ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, and self/doctor-reported angina). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001262 reports PGS-only AUROC=0.58683 and PGS R² (no covariates)=0.01304 with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint; its PRS-only R² is below the provided EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.009–0.014) but close enough to be plausible given scale differences, and it also has the strongest incremental AUROC (0.0098) among the snpnet siblings shown. Competing candidates either (i) come from the same pan-trait sparse UKB framework family with slightly weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS001260/PGS001261), (ii) lack PRS-only metrics and report only effect sizes with unknown covariates (PGS004457/PGS004527), or (iii) report only full-model C-index/OR from a benchmarking paper without clear PRS-only discrimination (PGS005047–PGS005059), making cross-model comparability limited. Overall, a direct-match exists but the pool is dominated by framework/benchmarking models and several candidates lack clean PRS-only performance reporting, so the recommendation is not high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. However, most are from framework/benchmarking contexts with limited PRS-comparable metrics: the UKB portability scores (PGS001876, PGS002089) report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), and the Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates, making PRS contribution and comparability unclear. The two snpnet models (PGS001267, PGS001268) provide the cleanest PRS-comparable evidence (explicit PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R², plus incremental AUROC) with basic covariates and European validation; their PGS-only R² values are below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling, supporting metric plausibility. Between them, PGS001267 is preferred because it targets the generic disease endpoint (not time-to-event packaging), while showing very similar discrimination to the TTE variant; remaining limitation is that both come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalizability risk), so the overall direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254; plus related aortic valve function measures PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases) and provides the strongest visible performance evidence among the direct AS models (reported C-index 0.87 in European validation) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). Main limitation: the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple comorbidities/risk factors), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated; this lowers confidence to Moderate despite being the most evidence-rich direct AS candidate in the provided set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for the target trait \"arthritis\" are present, including PGS001135 (\"Arthritis (nos)\", trait_efo=arthritis) and two additional arthritis-labeled models (PGS004477, PGS004547; both \"M13 (Other arthritis)\", trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful to the generic target (phenotyping_reported=\"Arthritis (nos)\") and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus full-model AUROC=0.67424 with a small incremental AUROC=0.00314, consistent with domain guidance that full-model AUROC should not be substituted for PRS-only performance. The competing arthritis-labeled models (PGS004477/PGS004547) report only an OR (1.1956 and 1.2622, respectively) with unknown covariates and no PRS-only AUC/R2, making them less directly comparable and less informative despite being direct matches. Overall quality remains sub-optimal because the best direct-match PRS signal for arthritis is weak (low PGS-only AUROC/R2 and minimal incremental AUROC), and the alternative direct-match models lack comparable performance reporting."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002727","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for asthma are abundant (66). Among the visible set, PGS002727 is a direct asthma PRS with a disease-focused pediatric-asthma framing and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.57, 95% CI 1.55–1.60) plus a full-model AUROC of 0.66 and R²=0.04, with very large validation sample size (n=391,820) and multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/SAS). This combination provides comparatively strong, PRS-relevant evidence (effect size magnitude) versus many other candidates that either come from pan-trait/framework contexts (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’ models) or report only full-model metrics without PRS-isolated evidence. Main limitation: endpoint fidelity is not perfectly aligned to generic ‘asthma’ because phenotyping is explicitly ‘Pediatric asthma’ and covariates are listed as ‘Unknown’, which lowers comparability and prevents a high-confidence selection over adult/general asthma endpoints (e.g., doctor-diagnosed asthma) that have cleaner phenotype wording but weaker or less PRS-isolated performance evidence in the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema). However, endpoint fidelity differs: three models (PGS003459, PGS003486, PGS004903) are explicitly for paradoxical/treatment-associated eczema in psoriasis patients, which is not a generic atopic eczema endpoint; PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (subtype/severity-restricted); and PGS002755 and PGS004587 target incident atopic dermatitis (closest to generic disease risk, though incident-only). Between the two incident-atopic-dermatitis candidates, PGS002755 is structurally stronger (PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage with 1,090,702 variants vs 23 GWAS-significant SNPs for PGS004587) and has a clear PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910). Key limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R² is reported for any candidate, so comparative performance is uncertain; additionally, the incident-only endpoint and reliance on HR(high vs low) rather than per-SD effect size reduce interpretability for generic atopic eczema risk."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005168","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in the provided context because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort atrial fibrillation meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) with a direct AF endpoint (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation) and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) plus a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663). Competing models either come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’, UKB portability) which domain guidance penalizes when disease-focused alternatives exist, or use horizon-/risk-calculator packaging (e.g., CHARGE-AF predicted 5-year risk; CHARGE-AF covariate inclusion) which is explicitly negative evidence for standalone PRS comparability. Remaining limitation: the reported C-index is a full-model metric with covariates including CHARGE-AF (a clinical risk calculator), and PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided here, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this keeps confidence at Moderate despite strong overall evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears either as the sole endpoint or as part of the combined AF/flutter endpoint). PGS001263 has the strongest endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both specifically 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517) that are sanity-consistent with the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), while using only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Competing models PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 use a broader combined AF+flutter phenotype (and PGS001339 is time-to-event), and the latter two lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 in the visible metadata (only partial-r), limiting direct comparability. However, confidence is not high because PGS001263 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known generalization risk per the provided domain guidance) and there is no clearly disease-focused multi-cohort atrial flutter-specific alternative in the candidate set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"High","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS000327, PGS002790). PGS000327 has the strongest endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder,” and it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS publication (Nat Genet: “Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”). It also provides supportive PRS-relevant evidence (OR per SD 1.33, and an R² estimate 0.0245) with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave) and EUR evaluation. In contrast, PGS002790 has a clear phenotype mismatch in phenotyping_reported (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”) despite the ASD label fields, and its reported partial R² is smaller (0.00546) with no effect sizes shown, making it less coherent as an ASD diagnosis PRS. Main limitation: neither model reports a clearly labeled PGS-only AUROC/PRS-only R², so performance comparability is limited; however, the endpoint coherence and stronger available effect-size/R² evidence make PGS000327 the best-supported direct match."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000452","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 20 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported PRS signal. PGS000452 (Cancer PRSweb, GWAS Hits, 28 variants) has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and shows the strongest visible discriminative evidence among the comparable direct-endpoint PRSweb siblings: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647), per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761), and strong top-1% vs rest OR 3.61 (2.53–5.15), alongside the highest reported Nagelkerke R² in this set (0.0487). Competing PRSweb models include near-ties (e.g., PGS000454 AUROC 0.632 with similar effect sizes; PGS000456/458 slightly lower AUROC), making the choice not uniquely determined. Newer Nat Commun models (PGS003416/PGS003417) are disease-focused and include MTAG (which is not a negative), but they lack comparable discrimination metrics (no AUROC/R² reported here) and have broader phenotyping_reported (“Keratinocyte cancers”), reducing endpoint fidelity versus the direct BCC endpoint. PGS005207 is explicitly restricted to childhood cancer survivors (endpoint mismatch for generic BCC risk). Overall, PGS000452 is best supported by the combination of direct endpoint alignment plus the strongest available performance/effect-size evidence, but confidence is moderated by the existence of very similar PRSweb near-clones and the absence of PRS-only (covariate-free) metrics across the pool."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002032","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo including “bilirubin metabolism disease.” Two candidates (PGS001824, PGS002032) have the most specific endpoint alignment (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), whereas PGS000924 uses a broader combined endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism (time-to-event)”) and comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk despite its reported AUROC/R². Between the two bilirubin-excretion models, the endpoint, covariates, training cohort (UKB), evaluation ancestry mix, and reported partial-r are effectively identical; with no PRS-only AUROC/R² available to differentiate them, method/structure becomes the main tie-break. PGS002032 (LDpred2; 19,768 variants) is structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than PGS001824 (penalized regression; 22 variants) given the same endpoint and evidence package. Confidence is not high because the key discrimination metrics (PRS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for both top-aligned candidates and the two are otherwise near-clones in the provided metadata."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches within the bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and similar basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), leaving limited differentiating evidence. For the target trait labeled broadly as \"bipolar disorder,\" PGS002786 has the closest trait_reported/trait_efo alignment (bipolar disorder) and the largest variant count among the siblings, which is a mild structural advantage when method family is identical. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly misaligned across all three because phenotyping_reported fields describe cognitive/behavioral measures rather than an explicit bipolar diagnosis endpoint, and the only reported metric is a small full_model_r2/partial R² (~0.0025–0.0031) without PRS-only metrics; these limitations prevent a high-quality direct recommendation and keep confidence low."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001033","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All three candidates are direct matches only at a broad/parent level, but none is a clean, high-fidelity match to the generic target “blood coagulation disease.” PGS001033 maps to the target EFO and is the only model whose trait_efo is explicitly “blood coagulation disease,” with reported PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS R² (0.0578); however its phenotyping is time-to-event (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalizability risk. The other two models (PGS001826, PGS002034) have a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint (trait_efo: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency) rather than the broad target disease class, and they lack AUROC/R² (only partial-r ~0.056), making them hard to justify as the primary direct match for the broad target. Given the endpoint mismatch vs broad target for PGS001826/PGS002034 and the framework + TTE limitations for PGS001033, the best available direct-match choice is PGS001033 but with low confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Multiple direct-match candidates are present for breast carcinoma (breast cancer/breast carcinoma). Among the visible options, PGS004153 is best supported because it is endpoint-aligned (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer) and comes from a disease-focused benchmarking study within the exact endpoint (not a pan-trait portability sweep), with no covariates listed (covariates=0), making its reported discrimination more comparable to a PRS-only setting. It also shows the strongest reported discrimination among the clearly PRS-centric candidates in this context (AUROC≈0.6625 with R²≈0.0764 and OR≈1.83), outperforming other strong direct-match options like PGS004040/PGS004025/PGS004083 (AUROC≈0.655–0.660) and older disease-focused scores such as PGS000332 (C-index 0.75 but with multiple non-genetic covariates) or PGS000007 (full_model_auc 0.78 with age/sex covariates). Main limitation: most candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index rather than explicit PRS-only AUROC, and covariate sets differ across studies; thus cross-model metric comparability is imperfect and lowers confidence from High to Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000316","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance reporting. PGS000316 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: \"Coeliac disease\"), is not restricted to a special subgroup (unlike PGS000041/PGS000042 which are limited to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers), and reports strong discrimination (AUROC 0.879 with CI 0.87–0.888) in a European validation. Competing disease-focused models include PGS000040 (full-model AUROC 0.90 but covariates are unknown and PRS-only metrics are not provided, so the AUROC may not be PRS-comparable) and several UKB framework/portability scores (PGS001301/PGS001856/PGS001894/PGS002067/PGS002107) which are penalized by their pan-trait/portability study archetype despite sometimes reporting PRS-only metrics. The main limitation is that PGS000316’s covariates are also listed as unknown and the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric rather than explicitly PRS-only, so comparability across candidates remains imperfect; this keeps confidence at Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003428","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among them, PGS003428 is from a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis study and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555), which is structurally favorable versus sparse/GWAS-hit-only scores and versus the pan-trait UKB framework model (PGS001299). However, the available performance evidence is limited and not PRS-only: PGS003428 reports only a full-model C-index (0.613) and an HR=1.33 (SE 0.069) with covariates (age, smoking), while other candidates show similar or higher full-model discrimination (e.g., PGS001299 full_model_auc 0.7676 but with weak PGS-only AUROC 0.552; PGS000073/PGS000784 full_model_auc 0.745 but are small 10-variant scores with HR~1.21–1.22). Because cross-study full-model AUC/C-index values are not reliably comparable and PRS-only metrics are largely missing for most candidates, the selection is not high-confidence, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004546","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (or a close composite including cholelithiasis). However, most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), making it hard to clearly identify a single best model on discrimination evidence. PGS004546 is selected because it is an exact ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis endpoint and uses an explicit multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which domain guidance flags as a positive structural signal; it also reports an OR=1.2986 per SD (moderate effect-size evidence) and is a sibling to PGS004476 with the same endpoint/setting but stronger reported OR. Main limitation: the Commun Biol 2024 models (PGS004546/PGS004476) have unknown covariates and no AUROC/R², while PGS001174 provides explicit PGS-only metrics but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (a known generalization risk) and uses a time-to-event phenotype; the portability-framework models (PGS001861/PGS002072) also lack comparable metrics beyond partial-r. This leaves residual uncertainty, so the direct-match choice is supported but not high-confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 22 candidates map to the target EFO (chronic kidney disease), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and study archetype. PGS002237 is the most directly disease-focused CKD model in the set: it targets clinically specific CKD stage ≥3 with an explicit eGFR threshold (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2) and comes from a CKD-focused publication (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries.”, Nat Med), with multi-ancestry evaluation and a reported effect size (OR=1.47) plus AUROC reported for a European validation record (0.78, though this appears to be a full-model metric). Competing models include (i) pan-trait framework/sparse UKB score PGS001272 (explicitly from the ‘813 traits’ framework and with weak PGS-only metrics), (ii) several benchmarking-paper siblings (PGS003988–PGS004158) with modest full-model AUROCs (~0.55–0.59) and a broader composite endpoint (“CKD or dialysis”), and (iii) models with endpoint mismatches or packaging (e.g., PGS000728 uses eGFR as phenotype; PGS000859 is tied to a diabetes subtype; PGS004224 is incident CKD in the context of secondhand smoke exposure; PGS004889 is incident CKD without diabetes; PGS005090 is AFR-only and may be population-specific). Main limitation: PGS002237’s reported AUROC is not explicitly PRS-only and includes many clinical covariates, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates from the visible metadata, lowering confidence from High to Moderate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates for COPD are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Among them, PGS001783 is best supported by the visible evidence because it is phenotype-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; ~884k variants), and comes from a broad multi-biobank development context (many cohorts listed), which domain guidance treats as structurally stronger than sparse/pan-trait UKB framework scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Its reported PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) is also within the provided heritability ceiling sanity-check (h2_liability ~0.0388), supporting internal plausibility. Main limitation: the candidate set is dominated by framework/portability-style studies and several models lack clean PRS-only AUROC; additionally, PGS001788 has the same endpoint/method family with a much larger validation sample but lower reported R2, and the Commun Biol J44 models report only ORs with unknown covariates, leaving some unresolved comparability and preventing a high-confidence, clearly dominant choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004621","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the disease level, but three are explicitly alcohol-related subtypes (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and one has alcohol-related labeling/variant selection despite a cirrhosis EFO mapping (PGS000776), making them less aligned to the generic target “cirrhosis of liver” than the two generic cirrhosis models (PGS000726, PGS004621). Between the generic models, PGS004621 has the strongest overall visible evidence package: phenotype alignment is exact (“Cirrhosis” with trait_efo “cirrhosis of liver”), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and it comes from a disease-focused cirrhosis genetics study with broad multi-cohort development and very large validation (n=1,153,995) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC/R²); the available AUROC values are full-model and therefore not directly comparable as standalone PRS performance, and PGS000726 provides only effect sizes (e.g., OR per SD 1.32; top-vs-bottom quintile OR 2.26) without AUROC/R². Given these limitations, PGS004621 is preferred but the direct-match evidence remains insufficient for a high-confidence, clearly best-supported choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002034","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both mapped to the target EFO and with identical reported/phenotyped endpoint text (\"Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)\") and similar basic covariates and ancestry context (UKB-derived portability study; DEV EUR; EVAL EUR/SAS). Reported performance evidence is limited to partial correlation and is essentially identical between the two (partial-r 0.0562 vs 0.0563 with overlapping CIs), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes provided, so performance cannot meaningfully differentiate them. Given otherwise near-clone metadata, the main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (32,552 vs 45), which is a moderate positive signal for capturing polygenic signal when other evidence is indistinguishable. Overall, this remains sub-optimal because both models come from a UKB portability framework context and lack stronger, PRS-comparable discrimination metrics for this rare congenital deficiency endpoint."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002042","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both explicitly aligned to the target trait with consistent trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = \"Corneal dystrophy\" and similar basic covariates and ancestry/UKB portability study context. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 or effect sizes; the only visible performance signal is partial correlation, where PGS002042 is modestly higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) with overlapping but shifted CIs. Given otherwise near-identical metadata, this small performance edge plus the more genome-wide shrinkage-style method (LDpred2) and much larger variant count (59,944 vs 38) supports selecting PGS002042, but the absence of standard PRS-only metrics and the shared portability-framework origin limit certainty, so the direct-match recommendation is sub-optimal rather than clearly high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000013","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Direct-match candidates are abundant (85) and many have strong phenotype alignment to coronary artery disease, but most report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with nontrivial covariate sets) and lack clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics, limiting a high-confidence single best pick. Among the visible candidates, PGS000013 is a clean direct CAD endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both ‘Coronary artery disease’), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (6,630,150), and provides an explicit PRS-only R2 (0.04) alongside full-model AUROC (0.81) with only basic demographic/PC/chip covariates—making its performance evidence more PRS-comparable than many alternatives.
